SMTO-EXE-0072 — The clipboard changed while SMTO was using it

GUID: f4f072f5-f4cf-5fb2-a492-d4674070c474
Slug: clipboard-stale
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: clipboard

What happened

  • Something new was copied on the Gateway computer between SMTO checking the clipboard and using it, so SMTO stopped rather than use or replace the wrong content. SMTO didn't change the clipboard.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Don't copy anything on the Gateway computer while SMTO is reading or setting its clipboard. A new copy in the middle of SMTO's step changes the content SMTO was about to use.
  2. Ask SMTO to check what is on the clipboard now and tell you, then confirm whether it should continue. SMTO then works from the current content instead of what was there before.
  3. If the clipboard keeps changing by itself, pause any clipboard manager or clipboard sharing on that computer, such as a remote desktop's shared clipboard. These programs can change the clipboard constantly, which makes SMTO stop each time.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reads or replaces the clipboard and reports the content you expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the Gateway's name, to the person who manages it. Don't paste private text onto that computer's clipboard while testing.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway clipboard's change token did not match the request's expected_change_id, or it changed between reading the content and the post-read check, so the operation was refused.

What this means

  • The supplied expected change token differed from the current token, or a supported token changed between reading content and the post-read check. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • The supplied expected change token differed from the current token, or a supported token changed between reading content and the post-read check.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare expected, before and after change tokens and backend token support; do not treat older content as a current snapshot.

How to fix it

  • Call clipboard.inspect to get the current change_id and decide whether a fresh operation is still wanted; pass expected_change_id only on backends that return a token and omit it otherwise. Check for clipboard managers or sync tools on the Gateway that rewrite the clipboard during reads.
  • Inspect current format metadata and decide whether a fresh explicit operation is needed. Use expected_change_id only on a backend that supports it.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the current clipboard and decide whether to proceed. Omit expected_change_id on backends without a token.

How to verify the fix

  • A new deliberate operation uses the current token where supported and obtains a stable result.

What not to do

  • Never automatically replay an uncertain clipboard write or include content in diagnostics.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
